name: Sardinia: Cagliari, Alghero, Costa Smeralda, Oristano

cities.base: Castello or the Marina below it: the museums, the cathedral and the Bastione on foot, and the trattorie of the Marina for dinner.
cities.name: Cagliari

cities.base: Inside or just outside the walls: everything in town on foot, the sea walls at sunset, and a car for Capo Caccia and Palmavera.
cities.name: Alghero

cities.base: Olbia old centre for the basilica and the trains; San Teodoro if it is beach weather. Either way you drive.
cities.name: Costa Smeralda: Olbia and San Teodoro

cities.base: Oristano's old centre by the Mariano II tower: the trattorie on foot, Cabras close by and Tharros 13 km out.
cities.name: Oristano and the Sinis

places.name: Sa Piola
places.note: Small Sardinian trattoria in the Marina lanes, 4.6 on Google from 1,910 reviews and about 38 euros a head on TheFork. It fills up, so book; lunch from 13:00, dinner from 20:00.

places.name: QuantoBasta
places.note: Seafood out in Sant'Avendrace, a ride from the centre; order the fried calamari. TheFork average 35 euros, rated 9.2 by 5,237 diners. Sunday is lunch with no dinner, and Tuesday dinner runs 20:30 to 22:00.

places.name: Duanima
places.note: Chef Luca Floris cooks seasonal Sardinian food in Villanova, 9.8 on TheFork from 562 reviews at about 40 euros a head. Dinner from 20:00, Tuesday to Saturday, and worth booking.

places.name: Antica Hostaria
places.note: Family-run since 1852 on Via Cavour; order the malloreddus or the fish ravioli at 15 euros. TheFork average 45 euros a head. On Sunday there is no lunch, dinner from 19:00.

places.name: Castello district
places.note: The walled medieval hill quarter of the Pisans and then the Aragonese, free and open at all hours. Give it 2 hours from about 09:00 and take the side lanes, not just the main streets.

places.name: Bastione di Saint Remy
places.note: The terrace on the Castello walls, 4.6 on Google from 28,090 reviews. Free and open round the clock; come at sunset.

places.name: Cattedrale di Santa Maria e Santa Cecilia
places.note: Cagliari's cathedral in Castello, 4.6 on Google from 4,996 reviews. Free to enter, 09:00 to 20:00 daily; allow 45 minutes.

places.name: Torre di San Pancrazio
places.note: The Pisan tower of 1305 at the north gate of Castello, with views from the top. Hours vary, check, and check the price at the door; 30 minutes.

places.name: Torre dell'Elefante
places.note: The 14th-century Pisan tower on the Castello walls; a 2024 visitor paid 3 euros to climb. One listing still flags it shut while its text says it reopened, so hours vary, check before you go.

places.name: Porta Cristina
places.note: A gate in the Castello walls next to San Pancrazio, free and always open; 4.5 on Google from 1,535 reviews. Walk through it on the way to the museums.

places.name: Palazzo Regio
places.note: The old royal palace beside the cathedral, 09:30 to 18:00 daily. Its listing says free but recent visitors paid 3 euros, so budget that; 45 minutes.

places.name: Museo Archeologico Nazionale
places.note: The island's main collection: nuragic bronzes, Phoenician, Punic and Roman rooms, finds from Su Nuraxi. 10 euros with the Pinacoteca, free first Sunday. 08:30 to 19:30, last ticket 18:45; closed Tuesday from 1 November 2026.

places.name: Pinacoteca Nazionale
places.note: The picture gallery in the same Cittadella dei Musei, on the 10 euro ticket shared with the archaeology museum. 08:30 to 19:30, Fridays to 23:00; the archaeology museum changes its weekly day off from 1 November 2026, so check this one too.

places.name: Museo delle Cere Anatomiche
places.note: Anatomical wax models in the Cittadella dei Musei, 4.4 on Google from 189 reviews. Listed 10:00 to 18:00, Tuesday to Sunday, but the listing warns hours conflict; check the price too.

places.name: Museo d'Arte Siamese
places.note: A small collection of Thai art in the Cittadella dei Musei, 4.5 on Google from 110 reviews. 10:00 to 18:00, Tuesday to Sunday; check the price, no reliable figure.

places.name: Galleria Comunale d'Arte
places.note: The city art gallery, 4.6 on Google from 592 reviews; a visitor paid 6 euros. 10:00 to 18:00, Tuesday to Sunday, about 75 minutes.

places.name: Roman amphitheatre
places.note: Cut into the limestone of the hill in the 2nd century BC. A 2023 report says works limit access and the 2 euro price dates from 2021, so hours vary, check before walking up; 45 minutes.

places.name: Tuvixeddu necropolis
places.note: Phoenician, Punic and Roman tombs cut into a limestone hill, 4.4 on Google from 1,525 reviews. Free, 08:30 to 23:30 daily; go in the morning.

places.name: Cripta di Santa Restituta
places.note: An underground crypt in Stampace, 4.4 on Google from 560 reviews. 10:00 to 17:00 daily, about 3 dollars on a combined ticket; 30 minutes and cool on a hot day.

places.name: MUTSEU Sant'Eulalia
places.note: The museum under the church of Sant'Eulalia in the Marina, 4.5 on Google from 520 reviews, about 7 dollars per its own site. 09:30 to 13:00 and 15:30 to 18:30 daily, so avoid the midday break.

places.name: Basilica di San Saturnino
places.note: A 5th-century early Christian church; free per visitors. 09:00 to 15:30, Tuesday to Saturday, so a morning stop.

places.name: Basilica di Bonaria
places.note: The Bonaria sanctuary, 4.7 on Google from 1,762 reviews. Hours vary, check, and check the price for anything beyond the church.

places.name: Castello di San Michele
places.note: The castle on its own hill north of the centre; visitors pay 4 euros plus 2 for a guide. Hours vary, check; take a taxi up and allow 75 minutes.

places.name: Fortino di Sant'Ignazio
places.note: A fort on the coast south-east of the centre, 4.6 on Google from 544 reviews. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Galleria Rifugio Don Bosco
places.note: A Second World War air-raid shelter, seen on a guided tour at 10:00 or 16:00 that you book ahead. A visitor paid about 30 euros for a three-site tour that included it.

places.name: Poetto beach
places.note: The city's 8 km strip of sand, free, 4.5 on Google from 3,981 reviews. Go on a weekday afternoon.

places.name: Su Nuraxi di Barumini
places.note: A nuraghe begun in the 17th century BC with a village of the 13th to 6th, UNESCO since 1997. Visits are by guided tour, every 30 minutes, every day; 8 euros. 09:00 to 18:30 in October, to 17:30 in November; 55 km, go early.

places.name: Casa Zapata
places.note: The museum in Barumini village, free with the Su Nuraxi ticket, 4.6 on Google from 2,045 reviews. 09:00 to 18:30 daily; do it after the nuraghe tour.

places.name: The Kings
places.note: A sunset terrace on the bastions; 4.1 on Google from 992 reviews. TheFork average 35 euros, open 11:00 to 23:30 daily.

places.name: La Saletta
places.note: Tasting menus, the dear dinner of the stay at about 75 euros a head on TheFork, 9.6 from 281 diners. 19:00 to 23:00, Monday to Saturday; book.

places.name: Osteria Macchiavello
places.note: Sea-view osteria on the bastions, TheFork average 31 euros, 4.2 on Google from 1,735 reviews; reviewers find the bill high for what it is. Open 10:30 to 22:30, to 23:00 on Friday and Saturday.

places.name: Trattoria da Mirko
places.note: A trattoria just outside the walls with the best Google score of the six, 4.5 from 2,387 reviews. TheFork average 35 euros; 12:00 to 14:30 and 19:00 to 22:30 daily.

places.name: La Cullera
places.note: Old-town restaurant on Via Sannino, TheFork average 35 euros, 4.3 on Google from 1,062 reviews. Closed Tuesday, dinner from 18:00 Wednesday and Thursday, lunch and dinner the other days.

places.name: Al Refettorio
places.note: In an old-town alley off Vicolo Adami, TheFork average 35 euros, 4.2 on Google from 2,227 reviews. 12:30 to 14:30 and 19:30 to 23:00 daily; book ahead.

places.name: Alghero Old Town
places.note: The walled old town, free and open; cars are restricted, so park at the port or on Lungomare Barcellona. Walk it in the evening, then dinner on the bastions.

places.name: Chiesa di San Francesco
places.note: Gothic-Catalan church on Via Carlo Alberto, tucked in an alley, 4.5 on Google from 600 reviews; check the price for the cloister. Mornings 09:00 to 13:00, afternoons to 17:30 early in the week and to 17:00 Friday and Saturday; closed Sunday.

places.name: Cattedrale dell'Immacolata
places.note: The cathedral of Alghero, 4.5 on Google from 1,793 reviews, 07:00 to 19:00 daily. No ticket price found, so check the price; bring a 1 euro coin for the lights.

places.name: Chiesa di San Michele
places.note: The church with the maiolica-tiled dome, 4.4 on Google from 301 reviews. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Torre di Sant'Elmo
places.note: A tower on the old town's walls, free per visitors, 4.6 on Google from 163 reviews. Hours vary, check; pair it with the bastion walk.

places.name: Torre di San Giacomo
places.note: A wall tower holding a coral exhibit, 4.6 on Google from 137 reviews. Visitors report it shut at odd times, so hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Torre dell'Esperó Reial
places.note: A tower of the town walls, 4.6 on Google from 1,722 reviews. Hours vary, check, and check the price if it is open to climb.

places.name: Torre del Portal
places.note: The old land gate, Porta Terra, 4.7 on Google from 45 reviews; a 2023 visitor joined a 12 euro walking tour from here. Hours vary, check, and check the price to go up.

places.name: Museo Archeologico della città
places.note: The town's archaeology museum, 4.4 on Google from 342 reviews, about 8 dollars. Split hours: Mon and Wed 10:30 to 13:00, Tue and Thu 16:30 to 19:00, Fri to Sun both. Check the day before you go.

places.name: Nuraghe Palmavera
places.note: A nuragic village abandoned around the 8th century BC after a fire, 4.5 on Google from 3,250 reviews. 5 euros, or 8 with Anghelu Ruju; 10:00 to 18:00 in October, to 14:00 from November to March.

places.name: Mercato Civico
places.note: The covered town market, 06:00 to 14:00 daily, 4.1 on Google from 1,745 reviews. Go in the morning; it shuts at 14:00.

places.name: Grotta di Nettuno
places.note: The sea cave under Capo Caccia, down 654 steps of the Escala del Cabirol or by boat from Alghero. Tours hourly, about 30 minutes, 10:00 to 15:00 in autumn, calm sea needed; shut on Thursdays from 12 November. 14 euros in 2022, check.

places.name: Capo Caccia cliffs
places.note: The cliff headland over the Grotto, free, 45 minutes. Do it with the cave and stay for the late light.

places.name: Torre del Porticciolo
places.note: A beach named for its tower, 4.5 on Google from 876 reviews, free; about 14 km from town, so you need a car.

places.name: Blao
places.note: Dinner on Via Mazzini, 9.4 on TheFork from 314 diners at about 35 euros a head, 4.5 on Google. 20:00 to 22:30 daily; book.

places.name: Trattoria Portixedda
places.note: The cheaper trattoria of the town, 27 euros on TheFork and 4.4 on Google from 1,928 reviews. 19:30 to 22:00, Tuesday to Sunday.

places.name: Il Lido
places.note: Fish on the Torre Grande seafront, 6 km out, 4.3 on Google from 1,819 reviews, about 36 euros. Lunch 12:30 to 15:30 every day; dinner 19:30 to 23:30 Friday to Sunday.

places.name: Estro
places.note: Rooftop terrace in Cabras, 4.7 on Google from 98 reviews, about 37 euros on TheFork. Dinner 19:00 to 22:00; closed Tuesday. Pair it with the Mont'e Prama giants down the road.

places.name: Torre di Mariano II
places.note: The north gate of the walls, built in 1290 under Mariano II; the Sa Sartiglia riders pass it at Carnival. Tickets are sold at a nearby museum, so check the price; hours vary, check.

places.name: Cattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta
places.note: Oristano's cathedral, 4.6 on Google from 1,071 reviews; check the price, none listed. Open to 20:00 daily from 09:00, 08:30 on Tuesday and Saturday, but from 11:30 Friday and 12:00 Thursday.

places.name: Basilica di Santa Giusta
places.note: A 12th-century Romanesque basilica just south of town, 4.7 on Google from 797 reviews. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Tharros
places.note: The Phoenician and Roman town on the tip of the Sinis, 4.6 on Google from 7,856 reviews and the reason to stay here. About 12 dollars, 09:00 to 19:00 daily; go at opening.

places.name: Chiesa di San Giovanni di Sinis
places.note: The church near Tharros, a 30 minute stop on the way in. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Museo Civico Giovanni Marongiu
places.note: Home of the Giants of Mont'e Prama, 8th-century BC stone warriors, boxers and archers reassembled from over 5,000 fragments. November to March 10:00 to 18:00, closed Monday; April to October daily to 20:00. Check the price, none published.

places.name: Mont'e Prama archaeological area
places.note: The dig where the giants were found, on guided tours a visitor timed at 09:15, 10:30 and 11:45, about 7 euros. Hours vary, check before driving out; see the museum in Cabras first.

places.name: Lu Brutoni
places.note: Wine bar and restaurant in San Teodoro, TheFork average 35 euros, 4.2 on Google from 741 reviews. Listed 19:00 to 23:30 daily, but a late-season opening is not confirmed, so check.

places.name: L'Osteria di San Teodoro
places.note: Central San Teodoro, about 36 euros on TheFork; 3.8 on Google from 1,002 reviews, with slow service the usual complaint. 12:00 to 15:00 and 19:00 to midnight, Monday dinner without lunch. Out of season, check it is open.

places.name: L'Ea Cana
places.note: Rustic Sardinian cooking at Monte Petrosu, 4.5 on Google from 845 reviews, about 40 euros. 12:00 to 14:00 and 19:00 to 22:30, closed Tuesday; book, and check late-season opening.

places.name: Basilica di San Simplicio
places.note: Olbia's 12th-century basilica over the tomb of the martyr Simplicio, home of the city's biggest festival. 07:00 to 20:00; one visitor paid 4 euros. 30 minutes.

places.name: Necropoli di San Simplicio
places.note: The burial ground beside the basilica, 5 euros with an audio guide. Monday, Wednesday and Saturday 10:00 to 13:00, so plan the day round it.

places.name: Tomba dei Giganti Su Monte 'e S'Abe
places.note: A nuragic giants' tomb just south of Olbia, free and open at all hours, 4.4 on Google from 901 reviews. 30 minutes on the way to San Teodoro.

places.name: Pozzo sacro Sa Testa
places.note: A nuragic sacred well on the edge of Olbia, free per visitors and open at all hours, 4.4 on Google from 458 reviews. Give it half an hour.

places.name: Nuraghe La Prisgiona
places.note: The best of the Arzachena nuraghi, 4.5 on Google from 3,067 reviews. 09:00 to 19:00 daily, 7 euros with Coddu Vecchiu; go at opening and do both.

places.name: Tomba dei Giganti Coddu Vecchiu
places.note: A giants' tomb a short drive from La Prisgiona, 4.2 on Google from 2,393 reviews. 4 euros alone, 7 on the joint ticket; 09:00 to 19:00 daily.

places.name: Tomba dei Giganti Li Lolghi
places.note: Another Arzachena giants' tomb, about 5 dollars, 10:00 to 18:00 daily, 4.2 on Google from 549 reviews. Add it to La Prisgiona and Coddu Vecchiu for a half day.

places.name: Nuraghe Albucciu
places.note: A nuraghe at the edge of Arzachena; a 2021 visitor paid 7 euros, so treat that as old. Hours vary, check.

places.name: La Cinta beach
places.note: The beach by the San Teodoro lagoon, free, 4.5 on Google from 8,443 reviews. Busy until mid-September; weekdays after that are calmer.

places.name: Spiaggia di Lu Impostu
places.note: A beach north of San Teodoro, free, 4.4 on Google from 5,096 reviews. Go in the afternoon after the nuraghi.

places.name: Spiaggia di Capo Coda Cavallo
places.note: The beach on Capo Coda Cavallo, free, 4.5 on Google from 1,082 reviews. Late afternoon, then dinner at L'Ea Cana.

destination.name: Sardinia: Cagliari, Alghero, Costa Smeralda, Oristano
destination.pitch: Come for the stone: nuraghi from the 17th century BC, Punic tombs, Pisan towers. Cagliari first, then Oristano for Tharros, Alghero inside its walls and Olbia for the Arzachena tombs, all with a hired car.
destination.caveat: Distances are long and the trains slow: Cagliari to Alghero is four and a half hours with a change, Olbia about four, and the nuraghi and beaches need a hired car. On the Costa Smeralda, check every restaurant is open outside summer; Neptune's Grotto needs a calm sea. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.food: Malloreddus at Antica Hostaria, open since 1852, Floris's seasonal menu at Duanima, fried calamari at QuantoBasta, the Alghero market in the morning and fish at Il Lido on the Torre Grande seafront.
because.nature: Neptune's Grotto under the Capo Caccia cliffs, La Cinta by the San Teodoro lagoon, Capo Coda Cavallo, and 8 km of sand at Poetto.
because.culture: Su Nuraxi at Barumini, the nuragic bronzes in Cagliari's archaeology museum, the Mont'e Prama giants in Cabras, Tharros on the Sinis and the Arzachena giants' tombs.
because.relaxation: Afternoons at La Cinta and Lu Impostu, sunset on the Bastione di Saint Remy, and a slow dinner on Alghero's sea walls.
because.exploration: Tuvixeddu's Punic tombs, the Don Bosco air-raid shelter, Alghero's wall towers one by one, the sacred well of Sa Testa and the dig at Mont'e Prama.
